nodes.description: YIPF5 is broadly expressed in the developing human cortex, in both the ventricular-zone progenitor and the neuronal compartments, most strikingly at 12 gestational weeks. Two model routes converge on disturbed cortical development: premature neuronal migration (mouse knockdown) and ER stress with reduced apical progenitor generation (rabbit knock-in). Neither has been examined in patient brain tissue.

nodes.description: YIPF5 binds the ER export receptor SURF4 and regulates the export of a subset of cargoes rather than ER export as a whole. In knockout cells, SURF4 cargoes and KDEL-bearing ER chaperones are secreted more, while several neuronal adhesion and migration proteins reach the cell surface less. Knockout cells also have lower ER calcium. Most of this was measured in non-neuronal MCF10A and HeLa cells.
